correctness.rationale: The all-prime valuation is a sum of level-wise counts of multiples, with every level above log_p(k) contributing zero to product-versus-lcm valuations. Above sqrt(k), exact Bernoulli variables are CRT-independent; below sqrt(k), their total logarithmic contribution is deterministically O(sqrt(k)). Weighted prime-number-theorem sums yield gamma and 2-log(2pi) by telescoping and Stirling. The variance constant is positive; the large-prime array satisfies Lindeberg and the small-prime term vanishes under standardization. Exact rational finite computations were replayed for 6467 cases; these are supplementary, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The classical Farhi quotient has known periodicity and exact finite value frequencies, yet its distribution under a uniformly chosen period as the window size tends to infinity is a distinct natural asymptotic question. The theorem identifies a nonzero universal fluctuation scale k log k, the explicit geometric-mean deficit constant gamma, a nontrivial variance constant 2-log(2pi), and Gaussian fluctuations. These are not mere parameter substitutions or a finite known-table computation.
